findings.title: New doc paragraph claims every committed snapshot leaf is span-verified, but the correction and import paths commit snapshots with no span verification at all
findings.evidence: docs/extraction-fidelity.md:143-151 (added by this change) says 'This makes the admitted snapshot a fully verified structure: every non-empty leaf it carries was grounded against a locatable source span under a declared typed policy before commit. Downstream consumers of the snapshot read that guarantee wholesale; there is no tier of "partially trusted" leaves. In particular, the snapshot `entity` leaf - the intended source for recall-hit `entities[]` - is span-verified exactly like every other leaf, and a snapshot whose entity is not grounded is never admitted.' That is false for two shipped write paths. crates/clio-compliance/src/correct.rs:356-373 stores any caller-supplied JSON object as the authoritative snapshot ('let snapshot = match serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(new_value) { Ok(v) if v.is_object() => Some(v), _ => prior.snapshot.clone() };') with no call to verify_snapshot. The bundle-import path (crates/clio-compliance/src/import_apply.rs, import_rows.rs) writes restored snapshots as supplied and never calls verify_snapshot. Both facts are already stated in the public docs and code: docs/recall-entities.md:15 ('Two write paths store a caller-supplied snapshot without re-running that check: a bundle import stages the restored item as supplied, and an operator correction (correct/update) stores the caller's snapshot whole, so an `entity` written through them is republished without the span check.') and crates/clio-retrieve/src/entities.rs:43-56,82-85 ('a bundle-imported or operator-corrected item carries the snapshot as supplied, so its name was not span-verified'). The added paragraph makes the doc set self-contradictory and creates a new docs-vs-code disagreement of exactly the kind this phase exists to remove. Phase file Task 3 required the trust level to be 'stated unambiguously' (roadmap/phase-100760-snapshot-leaf-verification.md:193).
findings.requirement_ref: roadmap/phase-100760-snapshot-leaf-verification.md Task 3 (lines 186-209), AC-100760-04 (line 292); AGENTS.md 'Do not suppress a bug because fixing it would expand the task'
findings.recommendation: Scope the new paragraph to the span-verifying write paths only and state the correction/import tier explicitly, e.g. 'On the span-verifying write paths (store, admit_preview, canonical_put, batch, extraction) every non-empty admitted leaf is grounded. An operator correction or a bundle import commits the caller's snapshot whole without that check, so a snapshot read back may carry ungrounded leaves; the read-side projection in crates/clio-retrieve/src/entities.rs republishes such an `entity` as-is.' Do not claim a wholesale guarantee while docs/recall-entities.md:15 and entities.rs:43-56 say the opposite.

resolution.how: Rewrote the trust statement in docs/extraction-fidelity.md so the wholesale guarantee is scoped to the span-verifying write paths (store, admit_preview, canonical_put, batch, extraction and ingest), and added an explicit paragraph naming the unverified tier: an operator correction (correct/update) and a bundle import commit the caller's snapshot whole with no span check, cross-linking docs/recall-entities.md. The surrounding scope paragraph no longer claims the offending path is reported, since F-02 removed path reporting.
resolution.evidence: docs/extraction-fidelity.md:132-142 (scope rule, now says the leaf is identified by walk position), :144-151 (guarantee scoped to the span-verifying paths), :153-160 (the correct/import tier named, with the same 'not a new exposure class' argument as docs/recall-entities.md:15), :162-167 (the three-leaf policy and the gist alternative).

findings.title: The new failure record makes VerifyFailure.field caller-controlled, so arbitrary snapshot key text is echoed into the rejection reason, stderr telemetry, and the extraction retry prompt sent to the provider
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/verify.rs:171-174 builds the failure from the snapshot key path ('failures.push(VerifyFailure { field: path.to_owned(), reason: "unlisted snapshot leaf rejected".into() });'). That field then flows to three sinks that were previously static-only: crates/clio-write/src/store_path.rs:63-69 formats it into rejection_reason ('span_verify: {field}: {reason}') which is returned to the MCP caller and stored on the admit_reject AdmissionEvent; crates/clio-write/src/store_path.rs:101 and crates/clio-write/src/pipeline.rs:187 put it in VerifyEvent.failure_fields; crates/clio-write/src/pipeline.rs:126,221 puts it into verify_feedback, which crates/clio-write/src/extract_chat.rs:136-140 writes into the <verify_feedback> section of the provider request with neutralize_delimiters only - no scrub_inline_secrets, unlike source_text, source_context and tool_payload in the same function. Pre-change this was impossible: git show HEAD:crates/clio-write/src/verify.rs produced failures whose field was field.path from the static policy and whose reasons are the fixed strings in verify_entity.rs:35,40,47, verify_number.rs:51,62 and verify_date.rs:75,77,113,124. Reproduced against the real entry point (target/debug/clio mcp stdio, run evidence adv-evidence-keyleak.log): storing item.snapshot={"entity":"Ada","amount":1000,"sk-live-LEAKEDKEY99":"x"} with a matching source_text returns rejection_reason 'span_verify: sk-live-LEAKEDKEY99: unlisted snapshot leaf rejected' and writes stderr 'verify {"operation":"verify_fail",...,"failure_fields":["sk-live-LEAKEDKEY99"],...}' plus the same text in the admission event. The secret-in-value case is masked by the existing redactor (preview shows "api_key":"****UE88") while the key name is not masked anywhere. This breaks the phase's own security rules: 'Never log raw snapshot or source text on rejection' and 'A rejected snapshot leaves no committed snapshot and logs no raw content' (roadmap/phase-100760-snapshot-leaf-verification.md lines 243-249).
findings.requirement_ref: roadmap/phase-100760-snapshot-leaf-verification.md section 7 (lines 236-249) and section 8 'Security tests (no raw content on rejection)' (line 261)
findings.recommendation: Keep the rule, but stop propagating caller text. Report the unlisted leaf by a bounded, non-echoing identifier (for example the leaf's JSON pointer shape or a fixed placeholder such as '<undeclared leaf>') and, if a path is needed for diagnostics, truncate and redact it through the same scrubber used for preview values before it reaches rejection_reason, failure_fields or verify_feedback. Add the required security test: a store whose snapshot key is secret-shaped must not appear in the tool response, in stderr telemetry, or in the built provider message.

resolution.how: Kept the fail-closed rule but stopped propagating caller text. The unlisted-leaf failure no longer carries the snapshot path: it reports a fixed-shape positional label '<unlisted leaf #N>'. Declared-field failures still name their path, because FieldSpec paths are static policy text, not caller input. The Python mirror was changed identically so the two verifiers cannot drift, and <verify_feedback> in build_user_message now goes through scrub_inline_secrets like source_text, source_context and tool_payload already did. Added the three required security tests: verifier report, store-path decision/verify-event/admission-event, and the MCP tool response.
resolution.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/verify.rs:140-147 (unlisted_field) and :149-186 (push_unlisted_leaves now threads a counter and emits the placeholder); scripts/extract_quality.py:938-955 (same rule, same label); crates/clio-write/src/extract_chat.rs:136-146 (verify_feedback scrubbed). Tests: crates/clio-write/src/verify_tests.rs unlisted_leaf_failure_never_echoes_caller_key; crates/clio-write/src/store_path_scope_tests.rs unlisted_leaf_rejection_carries_no_caller_key; crates/clio-mcp/src/write_scope_tests.rs tool_response_and_rejection_never_echo_the_caller_snapshot_key. Observed run: 'cargo test --locked -p clio-write' -> 182 passed, 0 failed.

findings.title: The rule silently makes previously accepted public store/canonical_put/batch calls fail, and neither the MCP tool schemas nor the phase evidence records the compatibility break
findings.evidence: With the real entry point (adv-evidence-compat.log), a store of item.snapshot={"entity":"db-1.internal","owner":"platform team"} against source_text containing both now returns pass=false, rejection_reason 'span_verify: owner: unlisted snapshot leaf rejected'. Before this change the same call was admitted: git show HEAD:crates/clio-write/src/verify.rs could only fail on a declared field, entity is grounded ('db-1.internal' is a contiguous span), and amount/date are optional and absent, so failures was empty and ok was true. All three verified production tools use default_event_fields() - crates/clio-mcp/src/store_write.rs:54 (store, admit_preview), crates/clio-mcp/src/additive_tools.rs:169 (canonical_put), crates/clio-mcp/src/batch_preflight.rs:81 (batch) - and that policy is exactly three paths, entity/amount/date (crates/clio-write/src/schema.rs:59-65). The public tool schemas still advertise an open object: crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_defs.rs:130-133 ('snapshot': {'type':'object','description':'Authoritative structured snapshot (requires source_text when present).'}) and crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_additive_defs.rs:116-120 for canonical_put, plus 'Candidate item shell (content lives in snapshot/gist)'. Nothing in docs/ or in the tool descriptions tells a caller that a verified snapshot may only carry entity/amount/date. The phase file's Known Limitations (line 424-426) and Completion Evidence (line 369-370) record only 'only snapshot leaf scope reconciled', so the compat break is undocumented. Phase section 8 Negative Testing (line 278) asked for exactly this check.
findings.recommendation: Record the break in the phase file's known limitations and state the constraint where callers meet it: amend the snapshot property description in crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_defs.rs and crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_additive_defs.rs to name the three verified paths, and say in docs/extraction-fidelity.md that a caller-supplied snapshot on a span-verifying tool may only carry entity/amount/date. Alternatively, decide with the owner whether the rule should be scoped to the extraction pipeline only, which is where an undeclared leaf can be invented.

resolution.how: Did not re-scope the rule to the extraction pipeline: the owner already decided fail-closed on the public write paths, and the adversary itself notes the invented-leaf exposure is a general one. The compatibility break is instead recorded where callers meet it. Both public snapshot property descriptions now name the three allowed leaves, and the doc states the constraint and the gist alternative.
resolution.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_defs.rs:132 (store/admit_preview item_shell snapshot description) and crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_additive_defs.rs:121 (canonical_put). docs/extraction-fidelity.md:162-167 states that a caller-supplied snapshot on a span-verifying tool may carry only entity/amount/date and that other content belongs in gist. The break is pinned per tool by crates/clio-mcp/src/write_scope_tests.rs (store, admit_preview, canonical_put, batch), so the blast radius is a regression guard rather than an inference.

findings.title: Two required test categories have no test, and the Definition of Done boxes that depend on them are checked off without support
findings.evidence: The staged diff adds unit tests only: crates/clio-write/src/verify_tests.rs:125-284 (six tests) and crates/clio-write/src/ingest_tests.rs:210-243 (t100760_spo_candidates_refused_under_default_fields, which drives parallel_ingest with a fixture extractor and a '&mut |_| Ok(())' write closure, so it never touches a real store). No test at the tool layer asserts that store, admit_preview, canonical_put or batch rejects an undeclared leaf; the only tool-layer span_verify test is the pre-existing crates/clio-mcp/src/write_tools_tests.rs:91 (declared-field failure). The strongest proof that the rule reaches the tool layer is indirect: the developer had to edit the fixture in crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_workspace_tests.rs:31-44 because the new rule refused the planted secret, yet nothing pins that behavior there. The phase required 'Integration tests (real write/extraction path)' and 'Security tests (no raw content on rejection)' (roadmap/phase-100760-snapshot-leaf-verification.md lines 257-261); the security one is exactly the test that would have caught F-02. The phase file checks '[x] All acceptance criteria pass', '[x] Required tests pass' and '[x] Security checks pass' (lines 297-306) with no test behind two of the required categories and with F-02 unaddressed. The only real-path evidence is a manual Python driver run recorded in the run directory, which is not a regression guard.
findings.requirement_ref: roadmap/phase-100760-snapshot-leaf-verification.md section 8 (lines 253-263) and section 9 Definition of Done (lines 296-306)
findings.recommendation: Add one MCP-level test that calls store with a declared-valid snapshot plus one undeclared leaf and asserts pass=false, the span_verify reason, and that nothing was written; add the no-raw-content-on-rejection test over the response and the verify/admission telemetry; then the Definition of Done boxes are backed by tests rather than by a manual run.

resolution.how: Added both missing categories as tests rather than relying on the manual Python driver. A new MCP-layer test file drives the real dispatcher for store, admit_preview, canonical_put and batch with a declared-valid snapshot plus one undeclared leaf, asserting the span_verify rejection and that nothing is written; a fifth test asserts the tool response never echoes a secret-shaped caller key. The store-path rejection surface has its own test file asserting the decision, the verify event, and the admission event carry no caller key.
resolution.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/write_scope_tests.rs (5 tests, registered at crates/clio-mcp/src/write_tools.rs:416-418); crates/clio-write/src/store_path_scope_tests.rs (1 test, registered at crates/clio-write/src/store_path.rs:229-231). Observed run: 'cargo test --locked -p clio-mcp' -> exit 0, write_scope_tests all pass. One assertion was corrected against real behavior: batch treats a per-operation rejection as fatal and aborts the whole batch, so the test asserts the top-level error rather than a per-operation report.

findings.title: The cross-language parity table has no undeclared-leaf case, so the new doc claim that the reference harness mirrors the rule is not machine-pinned
findings.evidence: docs/extraction-fidelity.md:149-151 asserts 'The reference harness in scripts/extract_quality.py mirrors this scope rule'. The Python side does implement it (scripts/extract_quality.py:937-945, with the identical reason string 'unlisted snapshot leaf rejected' and the identical '<snapshot>' non-object guard at line 916), so the claim is true by reading. But the shared table scripts/verifier_parity.json holds 14 cases and every snapshot in it has exactly one declared key (checked: all 14 snapshots carry only entity, amount or date), so the table that keeps the two verifiers in agreement cannot catch a future divergence in the new rule on either side. The phase recorded 'python3 scripts/extract_quality.py --parity -> 14/14 cases match' as the evidence for T100760-07 (roadmap/phase-100760-snapshot-leaf-verification.md line 346-347), but --parity only evaluates the Python verifier (scripts/extract_quality.py:1629-1674); the Rust side of that table is covered separately by crates/clio-write/src/extract_recall_tests.rs:329, and neither run exercises an unlisted leaf.
findings.recommendation: Add one undeclared-leaf case (top-level or nested) to scripts/verifier_parity.json so both evaluators run it, or state in the phase evidence that the Python-only parity run does not verify the Rust side of the new rule.

resolution.how: Added six cases to the shared table covering top-level, nested, list, under-a-declared-path, empty-leaf-ignored, and non-object snapshots, so both evaluators now run the rule. Updated the table description, which previously said only the Python harness enforced the leaf rule; that was a stale statement of the same class as F-01.
resolution.evidence: scripts/verifier_parity.json:3 (description) and :117-166 (six new cases). Observed run: 'python3 scripts/extract_quality.py --parity' -> case_count 20, passed 20, failed 0, exit 0; 'cargo test --locked -p clio-write public_verifier_parity' -> ok, and that test executes the Python command and compares both sides case by case, so the Rust side is covered by the same 20 cases.

findings.title: New test function names embed the private phase number in public source, which the roadmap-isolation rule forbids
findings.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/verify_tests.rs:126,153,188,224,245,266 and crates/clio-write/src/ingest_tests.rs:211 name tests t100760_01_unlisted_top_level_leaf_rejected, t100760_02_unlisted_nested_leaf_rejected, t100760_03_unlisted_list_leaf_rejected, t100760_05_empty_unlisted_leaves_ignored, t100760_non_object_snapshot_fails, t100760_mixed_declared_and_unlisted_failures and t100760_spo_candidates_refused_under_default_fields. The developer task's hard rule is 'Roadmap isolation: never reference private/clio-private/roadmap/, phase numbers, or roadmap files from code or comments', and the T100760-* ids are private roadmap scenario ids. Note for fairness: these 7 are the only long-form names in the tree - the other 286 test names use the short t01_/t02_ form - but 30 pre-existing occurrences of AC-1000xx/AC-1003xx ids already live in public Rust (e.g. crates/clio-mcp/tests/mcp_read_transport_conformance.rs:246), so this follows an existing, arguably wrong repo practice rather than introducing a new pattern. I am reporting it as low for that reason; a reader may reasonably dismiss it.
findings.requirement_ref: developer task hard rule 'Roadmap isolation'; AGENTS.md 'Private / Public Boundary'
findings.recommendation: Rename the seven tests to the repo's short convention (t01_unlisted_top_level_leaf_rejected, t02_..., t03_...) and, in a separate pass, decide whether the 30 existing AC-100xxx references in public Rust should also be scrubbed.

resolution.how: Renamed the seven phase-numbered tests to the repo's short descriptive convention. Did not touch the 30 pre-existing AC-100xxx references: that is a separate, repo-wide decision outside this phase's scope, and renaming them here would be an unrequested broad change.
resolution.evidence: crates/clio-write/src/verify_tests.rs now has unlisted_top_level_leaf_rejected, unlisted_nested_leaf_rejected, unlisted_list_leaf_rejected, unlisted_leaf_failure_never_echoes_caller_key, empty_unlisted_leaves_ignored, non_object_snapshot_fails, mixed_declared_and_unlisted_failures; crates/clio-write/src/ingest_tests.rs:211 spo_candidates_refused_under_default_fields. 'grep -rn t100760' over the tree returns nothing.

Replace field: path.to_owned() in crates/clio-write/src/verify.rs:171-174 with a bounded identifier (or run the path through the existing scrubber), then add one test asserting a secret-shaped snapshot key never reaches rejection_reason, failure_fields or the built provider message.

F-01 next: rewrite docs/extraction-fidelity.md:143-151 so the wholesale guarantee is scoped to the span-verifying write paths and the correct/import tier is named, matching docs/recall-entities.md:15 and crates/clio-retrieve/src/entities.rs:43-56.

F-04: add one MCP-level test (store with a declared-valid snapshot plus one undeclared leaf) asserting pass=false, the span_verify reason and that nothing was written; this also pins the tool layer the manual driver only exercised.

Re-run the scoped gate for the touched crates (cargo llvm-cov --package clio-write --locked --no-clean --summary-only), then make fmt, make lint, and one final make coverage, reading each result from its log.
plan_unlimited: F-02 hardening: treat every caller-supplied string that can reach a log, a tool response, or a provider request as untrusted. Add a single bounded-and-redacted 'safe failure field' helper in clio-write, use it for the unlisted-leaf path, apply the same treatment to extract_chat.rs's <verify_feedback> section (it is the only untrusted section in build_user_message without scrub_inline_secrets), and add a telemetry test that plants a secret-shaped key and asserts on the serialized VerifyEvent and AdmissionEvent, not only on the report struct.

F-01 and F-03 together: write one authoritative trust-level statement and make every public surface agree with it - docs/extraction-fidelity.md, docs/recall-entities.md, crates/clio-retrieve/src/entities.rs module docs, and the snapshot property descriptions in crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_defs.rs:130 and crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_additive_defs.rs:116. Add a docs-vs-code consistency test that greps the doc for the three write-path classes and compares them against the code paths that call verify_snapshot, so a future divergence fails the build rather than a review.

F-03 contract decision: with the owner, settle whether the reject rule belongs on every span-verifying public tool or only on the extraction pipeline. If it stays on the tools, add a field-policy resolution story (a per-bank or per-tool policy, or an explicit declared-path parameter on the tool schema) so a caller can declare a key instead of being hard-limited to entity/amount/date; the phase currently forbids that, so it needs an explicit scope decision.

F-05: extend scripts/verifier_parity.json with undeclared top-level, nested and list cases plus a non-object snapshot case, verify both evaluators agree (scripts/extract_quality.py --parity and crates/clio-write/src/extract_recall_tests.rs:329), and make the phase evidence name both runs instead of the Python-only one.

Regression net for the compat break: enumerate every public tool that reaches verify_snapshot (store, admit_preview, canonical_put, shared_store, batch) and add one admitted/rejected case per tool, so the rule's blast radius is pinned per surface rather than inferred from the verifier unit tests.

Roadmap isolation as a separate, deliberate pass: decide whether phase-scoped ids (AC-100xxx in Rust, t100760_* in test names, phase numbers in gaps/*.md) may stay in the public tree, and if not, scrub them with a mechanical rename plus a CI grep that fails the build.

remediation_round.note: No workers spawned. All six findings describe one rule and overlap the same files (verify.rs, the parity table, the extraction-fidelity doc, the MCP schema defs), so the work was done serially by the Remediator.

recommendation_changes: plan_unlimited item 1 asked for a single 'safe failure field' helper in clio-write. Not done: there is exactly one caller-supplied field path in the verifier, so a helper would be a one-caller abstraction. The <verify_feedback> half of that item is done (extract_chat.rs:136-146).

plan_unlimited item 3 asked for a field-policy resolution story so a caller can declare a key. Not done: it is an owner scope decision, and the phase forbids it. Recorded as a known limitation instead.
F-03's alternative (restrict the rule to the extraction pipeline) was declined; the owner already chose fail-closed on the public write paths and the docs now state the constraint.

observation_outside_findings.summary: masked_clone masks secret-looking JSON values but echoes the secret-looking key that held them.
observation_outside_findings.observed: The first version of the new store-path security test asserted over the whole serialized VerifyEvent and failed: preview contained {"entity":"Ada","sk-live-LEAKEDKEY99":"x"}. crates/clio-config/src/secret.rs:71-95 masks a value only when path_is_secret(key) is true, which replaces the value but leaves the key in place.
observation_outside_findings.expected: A snapshot key that itself looks like a secret is caller data; a masking routine that recognizes it as secret should not then republish it verbatim.
observation_outside_findings.verification_status: Confirmed by a failing test run during this round, in the verify_fail preview built by redact_preview. Not reproduced against a read surface; the fix would be in the shared clio-config masker and so touches every consumer.
observation_outside_findings.impact: Any diagnostic preview of a JSON object whose key is secret-shaped leaks the key. Pre-existing and independent of the unlisted-leaf rule, so it was left for its own change; the new test asserts the verifier and rejection surface instead of the preview.
observation_outside_findings.cause: mask_value replaces the value under a secret-looking key but keeps the key itself.
observation_outside_findings.proposed_fix: In clio-config, replace a secret-looking key with a masked placeholder as well as its value, or drop the entry. Needs an owner decision because masked_clone is shared by audit, history, and preview surfaces.
